$comment: The MCP servers this package registers, and where their entry point lives under
node_modules. One list, read by install.mjs when it writes ~/.claude.json and by
doctor.mjs when it checks they are still registered.
It was two lists before, and only one of them existed: the installer's. A server removed
from ~/.claude.json produced no row in the doctor at all, because the doctor enumerated
what WAS registered — the same blind spot the hook check had, in the same shape.
Local command servers only. A server addressed by URL is somebody else's service over the
network and every one of those ends at a login prompt; the doctor reports one as a policy
break, not as a broken install.

A server may be a node entry point under node_modules (`entry`) or a standalone executable this package does not vendor (`bin`). The second kind states where it installs itself and how to put it there, because a manifest that can only describe one shape quietly excludes the other.

playwright.why: the browser every render, audit and motion capture runs in

context7.why: up-to-date library documentation, so a version-stale API is not invented

codebase-memory-mcp.why: code structure the agent does not have to re-read the tree to learn: index a repo once, then search_graph / trace_path / get_architecture / detect_changes answer in milliseconds instead of a hundred thousand tokens of file-by-file exploration
codebase-memory-mcp.note: MIT, pure C, no language runtime, no API key and no telemetry — its README states it 'makes no network request of its own accord'. One shared coordination daemon per account rather than a process per session, which is why this one and not Graft; sources.json records that decision. `bin` rather than `entry` because this package does not vendor it: the `mcp` install step downloads the release asset for this platform from `install`, verifies it against the release's checksums.txt, and places the binary where resolveServerBin() reads (LOCALAPPDATA/Programs/<name> on Windows, ~/.local/bin elsewhere).
